title: Approximating a curve with ReLU units
sub: Gray: the target. Blue: a one-hidden-layer ReLU network. Dashed: individual units.

frames.caption: A target function on [−3, 3]. The universal approximation theorem says a network with one hidden layer of enough ReLU units can get arbitrarily close to it. Here is how.
1 unit: ReLU(x − b) is flat, then a ramp. Scaled and shifted, one unit can only draw a single straight line here.
2 units: each ReLU (dashed aqua) adds a kink where it switches on. The network's output (blue) is their weighted sum.
4 units: the first sets the starting slope, each of the others adds one kink. A piecewise-linear sketch of the curve, where every unit is just max(0, w·x + b) times an output weight.
8 units: the kinks follow the curve's bends.

32 units: max error 0.0145. Double the units and the error drops roughly 4×. So yes, one hidden layer is enough in principle; the theorem just doesn't say how many units, and in high dimensions that number can explode.
